items.title: probabilityStringMatch.js
items.box:
Andy, 2026-10-12: "Add one item: probabilityStringMatch.js"

The goal: three core modules in run/js, probabilit<Name>.js, built one by one; their integration argued after.

THE SPEC, Andy, 2026-10-12:
"probabilityStringMatch is to work like this

result probability = probabilityStringMatch(A,B) where A and B must be strings.

{

 function helperFoo1() // from old gradedSearch-logic
 function helperFoo2() // form old logic
 ... etc.

if A or B are not of type string return 0.0;
if A is EXACTLY equal to B return 1.0

shorterString = the shorter String of A and B
longerString = longer String of A and B

if they are of equal length, shorterString = A, longerString = B,

then use the logic from gradedSearch to return a result between 0 and 1

}"

DECIDED (Andy, 2026-10-12)
- "in this version, we just compute the matching of two string, no matter which one is the search string." So no wildcards: * and ? are characters like any other.
- The reading confirmed by it: both folded (case, accents); shorter and longer as the spec says; no match 0.0; else the weighted mean of gradedSearch's four signals (match 1.0, coverage 0.2, tokens 0.3, sequence 0.25), the helpers copied in, gradedSearch.js untouched until the integration.
- "and empty string against a non-empty string should return 0"

FOUND
- search today: bucket.js, searchBucket.js, gradedSearch.js, nodeSearches.js, peerSearch.js in run/js; a new file there is core, so its commit needs his grant.

checks.words: What should probabilityStringMatch do: given a query and a string, answer how likely the string is what the query meant, as a number from 0 to 1?

items.title: probabilityStringObjectMatch
items.box:
Andy, 2026-10-12: "new Item probabilityStringObjectMatch"

The goal: three core modules in run/js, probabilit<Name>.js, built one by one; their integration argued after. The first, probabilityStringMatch(A, B), is built (goal/G18.2, a9a0c252).

THE SPEC, proposed, Andy, 2026-10-12:
"this one we'll discuss a little bit

function probabilityStringObjectMatch(string,object){

1. the input must be valid string and object, empty string will return 0,

2. We "measure" the object
let table = [{objectString, weight]
function measureObject(){
// this internal function extracts every valid string from the object and places it in a table of objects, which contain the string and an empty weight (0.0) for staters
}

3. we assign weight to each string as follows: this is proposed and will be discussed.
the shortest string in the object gets the highest weight, the longest string in the object gets the smallest weight, and all the weights of the string in the table must add up to 1.0,

4. the overall input string is then matched agains all strings in the object, using pobabilityStringMatch(). each of those results is then multiplied by the weight of the corresponding object-string, and added to the overall result.

5. the overall result is returned.
}

thoughts?"

DECIDED, Andy, 2026-10-12:
"1. agreed. empty string stay out of the table.

2. no arrays are searched in this version.

3. dilution concern. when searching a table of objects, dilution doesn't matter because we look for the best matching contact not for the perfect one (this will become obvious in our 3rd item: probabilityBucket)"
- "nested objects will be searched for strings to put into the table."
- The weights: "you formula-correction is accepted." Each string weighs (S - L) / S / (n - 1), S the added length of all its strings, n how many; one string alone weighs 1.0; they add up to 1, the shortest heaviest.
- "if keys are string, they are included, this is supposed to be "dumb"": every key of the object and its nested objects goes into the table with the values (keys are always strings), empty ones out.

checks.words: How should probabilityStringObjectMatch work: a string against an object, for example the best probabilityStringMatch over the object values?
Weighted sum as proposed, or the best match?
And the weights: proportional to 1/length, scaled to add up to 1, is that your shortest-heaviest?
That, and still open: values only, or the keys too?

chat.text:
Added as goal/G18.3, your words in the box.
How should probabilityStringObjectMatch work: a string against an object, for example the best probabilityStringMatch over the object values?

Workable, with three gaps: empty strings must stay out of the table (shortest means heaviest, and they always match 0); does every valid string mean nested objects and arrays too, and the keys or only the values; and weight proportional to 1/length, scaled to add up to 1, is the plainest shortest-heaviest.
One concern: a weighted sum dilutes a perfect hit, so a name matched exactly among nine other fields scores about 0.2 and can lose to an object that matches everything weakly; the best weighted match would not.
Weighted sum as proposed, or the best match?

1. agreed. empty string stay out of the table.

2. no arrays are searched in this version.

3. dilution concern. when searching a table of objects, dilution doesn't matter because we look for the best matching contact not for the perfect one (this will become obvious in our 3rd item: probabilityBucket)

Recorded (v3): empty strings out, no arrays, the weighted sum stands since the bucket picks the best of many.
Open: does it go into nested plain objects, and are keys strings of the object or only values?
And the weights: proportional to 1/length, scaled to add up to 1, is that your shortest-heaviest?
nested objects will be searched for strings to put into the table.

Recorded: nested objects are searched, arrays not.
Two left: only the values, or the keys too (a contact {name: "ann"} would then also match "name"); and the weights proportional to 1/length, scaled to add up to 1.
Values only, and 1/length, yes?

for the weights of the strings:

1. the added length of all strings in the object represents 1.0
the weight of a single string is

 (sumOfAllSringLengthsAdded - stringLength) / sumOfAllSringLengthsAdded 

is this a viable formula?

Viable with one change: (S - L)/S over n strings adds up to n - 1, not 1 (lengths 3, 7, 10 give 0.85, 0.65, 0.5, sum 2), so each is divided by n - 1: 0.425, 0.325, 0.25, sum 1, shortest heaviest; with two strings it is already right.
One string alone gives (S - L)/S = 0, so a single string takes the whole weight, 1.0.
That, and still open: values only, or the keys too?

you formula-correction is accepted.

if keys are string, they are included, this is supposed to be "dumb"

Recorded (v5): keys and values both, nested objects in, arrays and empty strings out, the corrected weights, the weighted sum of probabilityStringMatch; every red Q here is passed.

items.title: probabilityBucket
items.box:
Andy, 2026-10-12: "add the third item: \"probabilityBucket\""

The goal: three core modules in run/js, probabilit<Name>.js, built one by one; their integration argued after. Built: probabilityStringMatch (goal/G18.2, a9a0c252) and probabilityStringObjectMatch (goal/G18.3, 6a4f7aa9). Andy on G18.3: "we look for the best matching contact not for the perfect one (this will become obvious in our 3rd item: probabilityBucket)".

THE SPEC, proposed, Andy, 2026-10-12:
"like bucket.js

the following differences 

1. function createProbabilityBucket(capacity)
2. seatFor(probability, item)

make sense, objecs are simply dropped into the the probabilityBucket with their probability, and probabilityBucket sorts that into it's table all by itself.

thoughts?"

DECIDED, Andy, 2026-10-12:
"The Bucket knows NOTHING about string matching, it will only know how to sort-add objects by probability.

internally its table carries objects like this: { probability, object }

the serialize will only serialize and measure the object portion of its array-entries.

make sense?"
- "the bucket fills up with objects of probability 0, until those objects are pushed out by higher-probability objects."
- "the ONLY job of probabilityBucket is inserting by highest-probability at the top, and limiting the serialized object, this way the bucket needs no compare-callback, nothing.

and the whole system is simpler,"

THE SHAPE, from those words: createProbabilityBucket(capacity) answers two functions and nothing else: seatFor(probability, object), which seats it by probability, highest at the top, an equal one behind those already in, and pushes the lowest out when full, answering whether it got a seat (a probability not a number or outside 0 to 1 gets none); and serialize(map, maxBytes), as bucket.js has it, over the objects alone, best first, cut at the byte ceiling, saying more and truncated.

HOW IT IS USED (the integration, argued after), Andy, 2026-10-12: "let's say: Desk Item search, the desk reads items, newest to oldest, up to MAX_SCANNED_ITEMS, compares every item against the search string, gets a probability as result, then drops the (probability,item) combination into the bucket. at the end calls serialize, done."
- Presence and nearness stay the peer search's: "The peer search will be able to weigh those extra concern on its own, and pass the combined probability into the bucket with the object, that additional concern is already handled today with the old version."

FOUND
- today bucket.js holds a fixed number of slots and evicts the weakest by a compare function; searchBucket.js and gradedSearch.js drive it.

checks.words: My guess at its shape: open it with a query string and a number of slots, offer it objects one at a time, it scores each by probabilityStringObjectMatch and keeps the best; how do you want it?
And should items() give the items alone, best first, or each with its probability?
And a probability of 0, outside 0 to 1, or not a number: turned away?

2. seatFor(probability, item)

Makes sense: no compare function, the probability is the order, highest first, an equal one behind those already in; seatFor(probability, item) answers whether it got a seat, and the rest stays as bucket.js has it (items, size, capacity, more, offered, serialize with its byte ceiling).
Two things to settle: is a probability of 0 (no match at all) turned away rather than seated, and a value outside 0 to 1 or not a number refused?
And should items() give the items alone, best first, or each with its probability?

The Bucket knows NOTHING about string matching, it will only know how to sort-add objects by probability.

internally its table carries objects like this: { probability, object }

the serialize will only serialize and measure the object portion of its array-entries.

make sense?

Yes: the table holds {probability, object}, sorted by probability alone, and serialize maps and measures only the objects; nothing in it knows of strings.
Left: items() giving the objects alone, best first, as serialize does?
And a probability of 0, outside 0 to 1, or not a number: turned away?
the bucket fills up with objects of probability 0, until those objects are pushed out by higher-probability objects.

Recorded: 0 is seated like any probability, pushed out only by a higher one.
My defaults for the last two, unless you say otherwise: items() gives the objects alone, best first; a probability that is not a number or lies outside 0 to 1 is turned away.
Agreed?

the ONLY job of probabilityBucket is inserting by highest-probability at the top, and limiting the serialized object, this way the bucket needs no compare-callback, nothing.

and the whole system is simpler,

Recorded, and the shape it gives is in the box (v5): createProbabilityBucket(capacity) with two functions only, seatFor(probability, object) and serialize(map, maxBytes), the second over the objects alone, best first, cut at the byte ceiling, saying more.
No items(), size(), capacity() or offered(): the bucket does its two jobs.
Is that the shape?

let's say: Desk Item search, the desk reads items, newest to oldest, up to MAX_SCANNED_ITEMS, compares every item against the search string, gets a probability as result, then drops the (probability,item) combination into the bucket. at the end calls serialize, done.

That is the shape exactly: the caller scans, scores and drops, the bucket seats and serializes; your example is in the box (v6) as the use, for the integration after.
Every red Q here is passed: ready for your Go, and the commit of run/js/probabilityBucket.js will ask your core grant.
do you agree that this is the better, or at least simpler shape? with these three little modules?

Simpler, yes, and better where it counts: three pure pieces, each tested alone, and the bucket holds no opinion at all, not even a compare; today that opinion is spread over gradedSearch, searchBucket and bucket.
Two costs to watch at the integration: the peer search also weighs presence and nearness, which the caller must now fold into the probability before seatFor; and keys count as strings, so short field names (via, name) carry the most weight in every object; measure that on real contacts.
Neither argues against the shape.

The peer search will be able to weigh those extra concern on its own, and pass the combined probability into the bucket with the object, that additional concern is already handled today with the old version.
Agreed, and recorded (v7): the peer search folds presence and nearness into the probability it hands seatFor. Ready for your Go.
